Tom —

Thanks — great questions. I pulled together two concrete options (attached) that we've used with other customers in regulated verticals:

Option A — Escrow-style amortization (recommended): upfront prepay is amortized monthly over the committed term; if the customer terminates early, remaining unamortized balance is refunded per schedule. This preserves predictable unit economics for both sides and aligns with our revenue recognition practices.

Option B — Pro-rata refund: a simple daily pro-rata refund of unused prepaid value (favors buyer but requires larger price concession up front).

About co-terming: operationally we offer a co-term checkbox on the SOW. Two typical approaches: (1) align the prepaid balance to the enterprise renewal date and amortize on the co-term schedule; (2) allow a short bridge period where the prepaid term is offset on renewal via a one-time credit. We outlined both with sample math in the attached PDF and an XLSX calculator.

Ramp discounts: we can model a 3-step ramp (months 1–3: 20% discount, 4–6: 10%, 7+ base price) and tie the amortization to the effective billing value. That means if you exit early, the refund amount reflects the discounted effective price for the months consumed. We included two sample waterfalls in the spreadsheet (pure amortized refund vs. amortized with ramp step adjustments).

Next steps: I've attached Redwood_Acme_PrePay_Proposal_v2.pdf and refund_waterfall_calc.xlsx — take a look and send any redlines. If you prefer, happy to run a short calc with your ramp profile and show CFO-facing numbers.

Tom / Lena / team —

Following up with a legal/ops framing and two concrete options reflecting your asks. High level: we can accept the 12-month amortization request but it requires a modest adjustment to pricing and the renewal credit mechanics. Below are the two workable paths and the operational implications: 

1) 12-month amortized refund (Acme-preferred)
- Mechanics: Prepay amortized monthly over 12 months regardless of prepaid term. If early termination occurs, refund = unamortized balance.
- Pricing impact: +6% effective price to offset increased refund exposure for Redwood on multi-year prepay.
- Co-term handling: if co-term requested, we create a balance alignment entry on the renewal date and apply any remaining balance as a renewal credit; the credit calculation will use the 12-month amortization schedule.

2) Escrow-style amortization tied to contract term (Redwood baseline)
- Mechanics: Prepay amortized monthly across the prepaid period (e.g., 24 months). If early termination, refund = unamortized balance.
- Pricing impact: no uplift; lower refund exposure to Acme.

Ramp discounts: we will enumerate three ramp tiers in the SOW and include worked examples in the SOW appendix. For refund math, the calculator will reflect the applied discount for each month and compute the unamortized effective dollar value.

Attached: updated refund_waterfall_calc.xlsx (tab "Acme 12m amort"), and a tracked SOW excerpt (PDF snapshot) showing the 12-month clause and co-term paragraph.

Action items for you: please confirm whether Acme will accept the +6% price uplift on Option 1 (12-month amort) or prefer Option 2 with no uplift but a longer amortization. Once you confirm, we will produce a tracked SOW for legal and prepare a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
